To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in salt-free conditions the dynamic properties of charged semirigid polymer chains differ from those of neutral polymers and that (ii) in the presence of added salt the ion-polyer coupling is only relevant on length scales smaller than the Debye length.

the length scale dependence of the dynamics of hyaluronan solutions is very different from that observed for neutral polymer solutions and that the ion-polyelectrolyte coupling breaks down at length scales greater than the screening length of the solution.
(1) D(NSE) is independent of the polymer concentration c and the ionic strength of the salt, and (2) D(DLS) decreases with increasing c, but increases with the ionic strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamic properties of charged polymers.
the dynamic properties of charged biopolymers in solution.
the dynamics of hyaluronan solutions, which is of great relevance in the field of biophysics, as hyaluronan is a major component of the extracellular matrix of connective tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ion-polymeric coupling is not present at all.
D(NSE) is the correct diffusion coefficient of hyaluronate in salt-free solutions, whereas the DLS diffusion coefficient is the correct one at higher salt content.
the length scale dependence of D(DLS) is determined by the interplay between the polymer and the solvent, whereas D(NSE) depends only on the polymer properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ion-polyelectrolyte coupling is only important at low q.
the length scale dependence of the dynamics of polyeletrolyte solutions is not governed by the ion-polyelectrolyte interaction but by the ion-ion correlation.
the length-scale dependence of the dynamic structure factor is determined by the length scale of the polymer chain, and not by that of the electrostatic correlations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ion-polyelectrolyte coupling is not the sole factor determining the dynamics of polyeletcrolyte solutions.
in salt-free conditions the polymer dynamics is controlled by a combination of electrostatic and hydrodynamic effects, which can only be resolved in neutron scattering experiments.
the length scale dependence of the dynamics of hyaluronian acid solutions is governed by the same mechanisms that control the behavior of neutral polymers.
